subject: THAPAR IN NEWS || Bringing Back Learning in Education by Prof. Padmakumar Nair
body:
[image: Untitled Design (7)]

THAPAR IN NEWS
Bringing Back Learning in Education
*by*
Prof. Padmakumar Nair
VICE CHANCELLOR,
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology, Patiala

Published on: 05 November 2026
Read the full article
<https://educationworld.in/bringing-back-learning-in-education/>
[image: WhatsApp Image 2026-11-11 at 17]
<https://educationworld.in/bringing-back-learning-in-education/>


For an enterprise called education, we spend surprisingly little time
asking a fundamental question: What exactly is learning? We discuss
curricula, credits, examinations, rankings, accreditation, placements,
infrastructure, technology, artificial intelligence and employability. All
of these matter. Yet I increasingly worry that education has become very
good at organising the machinery around learning while paying insufficient
attention to learning itself.

A student can attend classes, complete assignments, pass examinations,
accumulate credits and graduate with an excellent CGPA without necessarily
undergoing much intellectual transformation. That should concern us because
learning is not simply the acquisition of more information. It is the
process through which we revise the way we understand the world and,
occasionally, ourselves.
Read More <https://educationworld.in/bringing-back-learning-in-education/>

subject: Invitation to participate in Internal Qualifiers of GSC 2026
body:
Dear Students,

Greetings from VentureLab, TIET!

VentureLab invites expressions from undergraduate students to participate
in the *Global Scaling Challenge (GSC) 2027*, an international business
strategy competition organised by the University of New Mexico, USA.

The competition provides an exciting opportunity to work on real-world
business challenges, develop innovative business strategies, and present
solutions before industry executives and an international panel of judges.
Theme for GSC 2027

The probable focus area for this year's competition is *Nuclear Fusion*, an
emerging field with significant potential to transform the global energy
landscape.

Students will get an opportunity to explore its commercialisation,
scalability, business opportunities and entrepreneurial potential.
Team Formation Guidelines

Interested students are invited to register in teams subject to the
following guidelines:

   -

   *Team Size:* 3–4 undergraduate students.
   -

   *Faculty Mentor:* Each team must be guided by a faculty mentor.
   -

   *Interdisciplinary Participation:* Students from different academic
   disciplines are encouraged to collaborate.
   -

   *Team Composition:* Teams should ideally combine technical, analytical,
   research and business strategy capabilities.

How to Participate – Registration Required

*Interested students must fill out the registration form to express their
interest in participating in GSC 2027.*

Before submitting the form, students are encouraged to:

   1.

   Form a team of 3–4 undergraduate students.
   2.

   Identify a faculty mentor to guide the team.
   3.

   Nominate one member as the Team Coordinator.
   4.

   Submit the required team details through the registration form.

*Intent Form:* https://forms.gle/fF3CCTMbfQjSxpdm7

Please note that filling out the form is the first step towards
participation. VentureLab will subsequently conduct an internal selection
process to identify the most promising team(s) to represent TIET at the
international competition.
Important Dates
Activity Date

subject: Invited Lecture by Manish Gupta, ISRO Scientist on 5 November 2026, 3:30 PM
body:
Dear Faculty Members and Students,

The Department of Physics and Materials Science (DPMS), Thapar Institute of
Engineering & Technology, is organizing an invited lecture cum interaction
session on:

*“Journey to Venus: The Orbital Mechanics of Interplanetary Missions”*

*Speaker:* Mr. Manish Gupta
Scientist, U. R. Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), ISRO

*Date:* Thursday, 5 November 2026
*Time:* 3:30 PM
*Venue:* Ramanujan Hall, G-Block, Room No. 303

*About the Speaker:*

Mr. Manish Gupta is a Scientist at ISRO’s U. R. Rao Satellite Centre
(URSC), specializing in spacecraft flight dynamics, orbit determination,
and mission operations. With over eight years of experience, he has
contributed to more than 20 space missions, including the prestigious
Chandrayaan-3 and Aditya-L1 missions.

He has served as Project Manager for the RISAT-2BR3, RISAT-2BR4, and
RISAT-2BR5 missions, and Operations Manager for NISAR, XPOSAT, and
Oceansat-3. He also convened the Peer-Review Committee for the release of
Chandrayaan-3 Space Science data and has contributed to spacecraft orbit
modelling and scientific data archiving.

The lecture will introduce the fascinating principles of interplanetary
travel, including orbital mechanics, spacecraft trajectory design, orbit
determination, and the challenges involved in planetary exploration, with
insights from India's recent space missions.

All are cordially invited to attend this informative and inspiring lecture
and interact with the speaker.

We look forward to your enthusiastic participation.

With Regards

Dr. Bhupendrakumar Chudasama

Professor & Head

Department of Physics & Material Science

Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology

Patiala (PUNJAB)

subject: Leaving Personal Belongings in the Library and Occupying the Seats
body:
Dear Students,

It has been observed with serious concern that some students are leaving
their personal belongings, including study materials, notebooks, laptops,
and water bottles, on library tables to reserve seats for extended periods,
even when they are not physically present in the library. Such practices
result in the unnecessary occupation of library seating spaces and cause
considerable inconvenience to other students who genuinely require these
facilities for their academic and research activities. *The students are
leaving their belongings in the library, and they are coming to collect
their materials beyong library closing time at 10 PM. *

The library is a shared academic space, and its facilities must be utilised
responsibly, fairly, and with due consideration for the convenience of all
users. No student has the right to claim or reserve a library seat by
placing personal belongings on it in their absence beyond normal
situations. *A seat is meant for a student who is physically present and
using the library, not for personal belongings.*

In view of the above, all students are hereby advised to adhere to the
following guidelines:

   1. *No Seat Reservation:* Students are strictly prohibited from
   occupying or reserving library seats by leaving their personal belongings
   unattended.
   2. *Collection of Materials when Library is Closed: *If any student
   leaves their belongings and fails to carry them before closing of the
   library, the materials will be collected only when the library opens on the
   next day. Therefore, it is a humble request to collect your belongings
   before the library closes. *Please do not argue with the Security Staff
   in such cases. *
   3. *Carry Your Materials when leaving:* Students must carry their
   materials when leaving the library for an extended period. Keeping a seat
   occupied merely to secure it for later use is unacceptable.
   4. *Removal of Unattended Belongings:* Any personal belongings left
   unattended on tables, may be removed by the library staff to make the
   seating available to other users.
   5. *Consideration for Others:* Students must ensure that their
   individual practices do not deprive fellow students of the opportunity to
   use library facilities
   6. *Dignified Behaviour: *There are many feedback from the students
   about increased indecent behaviour and activities in the library. Such
   indecent and undignified activities create a disturbance for other students
   who seriously wish to study in the library. Therefore, students are
   requested to refrain themselves from such activities. Show compassion
   towards study in the library and not for indulging in undignified
   activities.
   7. *Compliance with Library Rules:* Repeated violations of these
   instructions may invite appropriate administrative action in accordance
   with the library rules and regulations.

Please understand that the library operates as a common learning
environment, and its resources and infrastructure are intended to benefit
the entire student community, not a select few. The library staff is
monitoring such situations, and necessary measures will be taken to ensure
the fair and optimal utilisation of available seating facilities.

Your cooperation in maintaining a disciplined, equitable, and
student-friendly learning environment is expected and much appreciated. In
case you have any suggestions in these matters, you are most welcome to
reach us.
-- 

With Regards,

*Shri Ram*

subject: Re: 🏆 Exciting Prize Challenge! AI-Powered Engineering/Educational Video Lecture Challenge – Win up to ₹6,000!
body:
Dear Faculty Members, Staff Members, and Students (Phd/PG/UG),

Greetings from the Dean's Office, Digital Content Transformation (DCT)!

We are pleased to announce the *AI-Powered Engineering Video Lecture
Challenge*, an initiative to encourage creativity, innovation, and the
effective use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in engineering education and
digital content creation.

All faculty members, staff members, UG/PG students, and Ph.D. scholars are
invited to participate in this exciting challenge.

*Challenge Theme:*
Create a *10-minute educational video lecture* on any engineering topic
that addresses real-world challenges and demonstrates its relevance and
potential benefits to society.

*Participation Guidelines:*

   -

   Each team must consist of *exactly 3 members*.
   -

   Teams can include UG/PG students, Ph.D. scholars, faculty members, and
   staff members in any combination.
   -

   The video must include the team's own video/audio narration, relevant
   visuals, animations, and effective use of AI tools.
   -

   The content should be technically accurate, engaging, innovative, and
   socially relevant.
   -

   Interdisciplinary and collaborative teams are highly encouraged.

*Exciting Prizes**:*

🏆 First Prize (worth)  : *₹6,000 *

🥈 Second Prize (worth) : *₹4,500*

🥉 Third Prize (worth): *₹3,000*

*Evaluation Criteria:*
Submissions will be evaluated based on technical accuracy, societal
relevance, creativity, quality of audio-visual presentation, animation, and
effective use of AI tools.

This is an excellent opportunity to showcase your technical knowledge,
creativity, communication skills, and AI-powered content creation
capabilities while developing educational resources that can benefit the
wider community.

*Registration and Submission:*
Registration link: https://forms.gle/2MAnxCQuwS116uKF6

Last date for registration: 05/11/2026

Last date for video submission: 20/11/2026 (Submission link will be shared
later to the registered participants)

For detailed competition guidelines, eligibility requirements, and
submission instructions, please refer to the attached document.

We encourage all faculty members, staff members, and students to
participate enthusiastically and make this initiative a grand
success. Participants are also encouraged to make use of the *Digital
Content Transformation (DCT) Studio*, TIET, for professional video
recording, audio recording and video editing wherever required.

Let's use technology and creativity to transform engineering education and
create a positive impact on society!

Best Regards,

*Dean's Office*
Digital Content Transformation (DCT)
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology (TIET), Patiala

body:
Dear Faculty Members, Staff Members, and Students (Phd/PG/UG),

Greetings from the Dean's Office, Digital Content Transformation (DCT)!

We are pleased to announce the *AI-Powered Engineering Video Lecture
Challenge*, an initiative to encourage creativity, innovation, and the
effective use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in engineering education and
digital content creation.

All faculty members, staff members, UG/PG students, and Ph.D. scholars are
invited to participate in this exciting challenge.

*Challenge Theme:*
Create a *10-minute educational video lecture* on any engineering topic
that addresses real-world challenges and demonstrates its relevance and
potential benefits to society.

*Participation Guidelines:*

   -

   Each team must consist of *exactly 3 members*.
   -

   Teams can include UG/PG students, Ph.D. scholars, faculty members, and
   staff members in any combination.
   -

   The video must include the team's own video/audio narration, relevant
   visuals, animations, and effective use of AI tools.
   -

   The content should be technically accurate, engaging, innovative, and
   socially relevant.
   -

   Interdisciplinary and collaborative teams are highly encouraged.

*Exciting Prizes**:*

🏆 First Prize (worth)  : *₹6,000 *

🥈 Second Prize (worth) : *₹4,500*

🥉 Third Prize (worth): *₹3,000*

*Evaluation Criteria:*
Submissions will be evaluated based on technical accuracy, societal
relevance, creativity, quality of audio-visual presentation, animation, and
effective use of AI tools.

This is an excellent opportunity to showcase your technical knowledge,
creativity, communication skills, and AI-powered content creation
capabilities while developing educational resources that can benefit the
wider community.

*Registration and Submission:*
Registration link: https://forms.gle/2MAnxCQuwS116uKF6

Last date for registration: 04/11/2026

Last date for video submission: 20/11/2026 (Submission link will be shared
later to the registered participants)

For detailed competition guidelines, eligibility requirements, and
submission instructions, please refer to the attached document.

We encourage all faculty members, staff members, and students to
participate enthusiastically and make this initiative a grand
success. Participants are also encouraged to make use of the *Digital
Content Transformation (DCT) Studio*, TIET, for professional video
recording, audio recording and video editing wherever required.

Let's use technology and creativity to transform engineering education and
create a positive impact on society!

Best Regards,

*Dean's Office*
Digital Content Transformation (DCT)
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology (TIET), Patiala

Dear everyone,

Some evenings deserve to be set apart from the hurried rhythm of everyday
life; evenings of good company, stirring melodies, and music that lingers
long after the last
note fades.

With this thought, we invite you to Jashn-e-Mehfil, an evening where
timeless traditions meet soulful melodies, and music becomes a language of
its own.

Taking the stage is Tabish Pasha, whose soulful voice promises an evening
of melodies that resonate beyond words. Through his music, expect a
gathering filled with warmth, familiar emotions, and moments that stay with
you long after the evening draws to a
close.

SPICMACAY presents Dhruv Bedi, whose artistry on the sitar brings the
richness of Indian classical music to the forefront. Through intricate
melodies and the timeless language of ragas, his performance promises an
immersive experience celebrating
India’s classical heritage and the beauty of its musical traditions.

Adding to the evening, a special performance awaits, bringing another shade
of expression to this celebration of music.

*Jashn-e-Mehfil*
*Date:* 28 October 2026
*Venue:* Open Air Theatre (OAT)
*Dress Code:* Ethnic
*Entry Timings:*
•⁠ ⁠5:30 PM onwards: For attendees with an issued pass.
•⁠ ⁠6:00 PM onwards: For other attendees.

*Important Guidelines for Attendees*
- Valid identification is mandatory.
- ⁠Carry your TIET Identity Card or Admission Letter. Entry will not be
permitted without valid identification.
- ⁠No baggage or belongings will be permitted inside the event premises.
- ⁠Only sealed water bottles are allowed inside the venue.
- ⁠Outside food and edibles are prohibited.
- ⁠Please cooperate with the volunteers and organising team of Saturnalia
and follow all instructions throughout the event.
- ⁠Entry and exit will be managed by the organising team and security.
Please follow their instructions.
- ⁠If an individual leaves the venue once entry won’t be allowed again.

Please arrive according to your designated entry time and keep your pass
ready, where
applicable, for a smooth entry.
Bring your friends along, step away from the everyday, and join us for an
evening where every melody has a moment of its own.

इंतज़ार रहेगा, इस शाम आपसे मिलने का।

Warmly,
Team Saturnalia
